6.1.3 RELATION OF BIOLOGY WITH OTHER SCIENCE The exploration of life science involves knowledge of other basic sciences like Physics and Chemistry. The combination of these disciplines contributes to a comprehensive perspective.

Relation with Chemistry The physiological processes of plants and animals are intricately linked with chemical reactions. Biochemistry, situated at the intersection of Biology and Chemistry, is the discipline that addresses this intersection. Biology is related with Chemistry, because of the following reasons:
Figure 6.2 Photosynthesis vs. Cellular respiration Biology, Grade 11 | 233
a. Living organisms contain both organic and inorganic compounds, which play a crucial role in shaping various life processes.
b. Energy is transferred within the body through organic chemicals like glucose. c. Chemical changes are integral to metabolic pathways, including photosynthesis,

respiration, and metabolism. d. Genetic materials such as DNA and RNA are composed of chemicals. e. Enzymes and hormones secreted in animals are exclusively chemical in nature. Relation with Physics Biology is related with the Physics, because of the following reasons:

Figure 6.3 Compound Microscope a. Some life processes such as sap movement, diffusion, mineral transport, etc. rely on physical phenomena. b. Many tools in biology, such as microscopes, chromatography, X-ray diffraction, etc. use physical principles. c. The physiological activities of plants depend on factors like light intensity and energy. d. Working of eyes is based on the principle of optics.
